title: Pushouts along an open immersion and a separated etale map
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $Z,V$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $j:W\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open subspace [def-a1-space-open-subspace], and let $q:W\to V$ be an $S$-morphism which is etale in the chartwise sense [def-sfb-space-chartwise-etale-morphism] and separated: its diagonal is representable and becomes a closed immersion after every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion]. There exist an algebraic space $Y/S$ and $S$-morphisms $a:Z\to Y$, $b:V\to Y$ such that $aj=bq$, $b$ identifies $V$ with an open subspace of $Y$, $a$ is chartwise etale, and the canonical map $W\to Z\times_YV$ is an isomorphism [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. If $T\hookrightarrow Y$ is the reduced closed subspace supported on $|Y|\setminus|V|$, with the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology, lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support], then $Z\times_YT\to T$ is an isomorphism. The square is a pushout in algebraic spaces over $S$: for every algebraic space $H/S$, compatible maps $Z\to H$ and $V\to H$ agreeing on $W$ factor uniquely through $Y$. No affineness, Noetherian, quasi-compactness, or finite type hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0DVJ (lemma-construct-elementary-distinguished-square), full statement; the conditions of an elementary distinguished square are written out.

proof.text: Put $P=W\times_VW$. Its projections to $W$ are chartwise etale by base change of $q$. The diagonal $\delta:W\to P$ is a monomorphism of sheaves, and is chartwise etale: both $W\to W$ and $P\to W$ are chartwise etale, so apply etale permanence to this morphism over $W$. The etale-monomorphism lemma makes $\delta$ an open immersion. The hypothesis on $q$ also makes it a closed immersion. Consequently $E=P\setminus\delta(W)$ is an open subspace, and $P=\delta(W)\amalg E$. This is a statement about subfunctors: on a scheme test the two inverse images are complementary clopen subschemes. Form the algebraic spaces $A=V\amalg Z$ and $R=V\amalg W\amalg W\amalg Z\amalg E$. These are finite coproducts; finite coproducts of their scheme atlases are within the fixed universes. Their coprojections are open immersions by the clopen-partition description of sheaf coproducts. Define $(s,t):R\to A\times_S A$ on its five summands by $(v,v)$, $(q(w),j(w))$, $(j(w),q(w))$, $(z,z)$, and $(j(w_1),j(w_2))$, respectively.

Check the relation on a clopen cover of a test scheme where each section has a fixed $V$- or $Z$-label. In the $VV$ component it is equality. In the $VZ$ component it consists of pairs $(q(w),j(w))$, and in $ZV$ of the reversed pairs. In $ZZ$ it is equality on $Z$, together with unequal pairs of points of $W$ having the same $q$-image. The last assertion uses $P=\delta(W)\amalg E$: even for a family that is equal on only part of the test scheme, that part and its complement are clopen. Each pair thus has at most one representing relation section. Reflexivity is the $V$ and $Z$ diagonal summands, and symmetry exchanges the two $W$ summands and the coordinates of $E$. For transitivity, a chain meeting a $V$-label has all its $Z$-labels in $W$ and all its $V$-labels equal to their common $q$-image; its endpoints are therefore related. A chain wholly in $Z$ either contains an equality, or has all entries in $W$ with a common $q$-image, so has related endpoints as well. Uniqueness lets the local relation sections glue. Hence $(s,t)$ is monic and $R(H)$ is an equivalence relation on $A(H)$ for every test scheme $H$.

The maps $s,t$ are chartwise etale. On the five summands their maps to the relevant component of $A$ are identities, $q$, $j$, or $E\to P\to W\xrightarrow{j}Z$. Open immersions are chartwise etale by the open-chart test, and the two projections $P\to W$ are base changes of $q$. Thus all these component maps are chartwise etale by permanence. To check the finite union assertion rather than assume it, take a representable etale scheme chart $B\to R$. The clopen-partition lemma decomposes $B$ into five clopen schemes $B_i$. Each $B_i\to R_i$ is a representable etale chart, by base change and composition with the open coprojection. Thus $B_i\to A$ is representable etale. On any scheme test $C\to A$, the pullback of $B\to A$ is the finite scheme coproduct of the etale schemes $C\times_A B_i$; the finite-coproduct etale lemma makes its map to $C$ etale. This verifies exactly the definition of chartwise etaleness for $s,t$.

Apply the effective etale-relation quotient theorem to $R\rightrightarrows A$. Its hypotheses were checked in Steps 2 and 3. Obtain the algebraic space $Y=A/R$ and the chartwise etale quotient map $p:A\to Y$, with etale-local lifts and $A\times_Y A=R$. Write $b=p|_V$ and $a=p|_Z$. The two $W$ components of the kernel pair give $bq=aj$. This is the actual sheafified quotient of the explicitly constructed relation, not an arbitrary choice of an algebraic space.

The coprojections $V,Z\to A$ are open, hence chartwise etale by the open-chart test. Composing with $p$ shows that both $a,b$ are chartwise etale. Restricting the kernel-pair isomorphism to the $VV$ component gives $V\times_YV=V$ with both projections the identity. Thus $b$ is a monomorphism of sheaves, and the etale-monomorphism lemma makes $b$ an open immersion. Restricting instead to the $ZV$ component gives $Z\times_YV=W$, with projections $j,q$. In particular this is the canonical map $W\to Z\times_YV$, not merely an unspecified isomorphism of spaces.

Let $T\hookrightarrow Y$ be the reduced closed subspace with support $|Y|\setminus|V|$, supplied by the reduced-closed-support theorem. The point-space pullback formula shows $V\times_YT$ has no points, so it is empty (a nonempty scheme atlas would have a point). The same holds for $W\times_YT$, since $aj=bq$. Pulling the quotient's etale-local lifts back to a scheme over $T$ therefore gives local lifts to $Z\times_YT$: the $V$-label is impossible. In the $ZZ$ part of the kernel relation, the $E$ summand vanishes after this base change because its endpoints factor through $W$; only the diagonal $Z$ summand remains. Hence $Z\times_YT\to T$ is monic and every scheme-test section lifts etale locally. These local lifts are unique and agree on overlaps, so the sheaf condition glues them to a unique global lift. This constructs an inverse as a natural transformation, proving $Z\times_YT\simeq T$. The argument works over any space disjoint from $V$; it does not assume that a base change of $T$ remains reduced.

For an algebraic space $H/S$, let $g:Z\to H$ and $h:V\to H$ satisfy $gj=hq$. The coproduct map $u=h\amalg g:A\to H$ equalizes $s,t$: on the $V,Z$ diagonals this is tautological, on each $W$ summand it is the given compatibility, and on $E$ one has $gj(w_1)=hq(w_1)=hq(w_2)=gj(w_2)$ because $q(w_1)=q(w_2)$. The quotient universal property therefore supplies a unique map $Y\to H$ restricting to $g,h$. Conversely every such map gives the compatibility since $aj=bq$. All maps and quotients were taken over $S$, so this proves the required pushout in algebraic spaces over $S$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q70-4b17ffd0b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item (7 steps), the new node lem-per-space-etale-relation-quotient, every cited statement, and the sources Stacks 0DVJ, its preceding pushout lemma, 04S6(1) and 046O. The item statement is byte-identical to the base (checked against the NL snapshot) and is the full 0DVJ statement, conditions included, not weakened. The steps follow Stacks' five-summand relation. Step 1: diagonal open by the etale-monomorphism lemma and closed by separatedness, P=δ(W)⊔E, coproducts algebraic. Step 2 (marked elementary, the source's 'immediately verified'): monic and an equivalence relation, checked by clopen pieces; this is justified. Step 3: s,t chartwise etale through the clopen split of a chart and the finite scheme-coproduct etale lemma. Steps 4-7: the open embedding and the canonical iso W≅Z×_YV come from the kernel pair; Z×_YT≅T because V×_YT, W×_YT and E×_YT are empty, with gluing of etale-local lifts; the pushout comes from the quotient's universal property and u equalizes s,t, including on E. The new node is true: 04S6(1); 046O plus monicity gives the kernel pair; p is representable and etale; etale-local lifting holds. It was tested on R=A, A=∅ and the scheme case. It is not a duplicate: lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient and the related trf/sfb quotient nodes are for schemes only, and the bootstrap nodes start from a given sheaf. It does not restate an item clause. Batch-5: the cited trf/a1/sfb nodes are general definitions and foundational facts about algebraic spaces (fibre products, coproducts, partition of sheaf coproducts, etale permanence, open charts, point images, etale monomorphisms open), outside the trace-formula and Poincaré-duality statements and not steps of their proofs. Accepted. Tool uses of generic geometry from units sk-p-real-rankin, sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability, sk-i-curve-zero and sk-prop-h2 accepted. No SGA citation. lean.statement: theorem exists_openSeparatedEtalePushout {S : Scheme.{u}} (W Z V : AlgebraicSpace S) (j : W ⟶ Z) (q : W ⟶ V) (hj : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) j.hom.hom) (hq : IsChartwiseEtale q) (hsep : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (pullback.diagonal q.hom.hom)) : ∃ (Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (a : Z ⟶ Y) (b : V ⟶ Y), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) b.hom.hom ∧ IsChartwiseEtale a ∧ IsPullback j.hom q.hom a.hom b.hom ∧ (∀ C : ClosedSubspace Y, IsReduced (C.val : AlgebraicSpace S) → pointImage C.val.arrow.hom.hom = (pointImage b.hom.hom)ᶜ → IsIso (Limits.pullback.snd a.hom C.val.arrow.hom)) ∧ ∀ (H : AlgebraicSpace S) (g : Z ⟶ H) (h : V ⟶ H), j ≫ g = q ≫ h → ∃! t : Y ⟶ H, a ≫ t = g ∧ b ≫ t = h

reviewed_lean.note: Read node, Stacks 0DVJ, all stmt_dep declarations (IsRepresentableWith, OpenSubspace, IsChartwiseEtale, pointImage, ClosedSubspace, IsReduced, exists_unique_reduced_closed_subspace, fibreProduct_isAlgebraicSpace) and the delivered module. Every clause matches: open j as the OpenSubspace predicate on a morphism; chartwise-etale q; separatedness as closed-immersion representability of the relative diagonal pullback.diagonal q; IsPullback j q a b gives aj=bq and the canonical W≅Z×_YV; b open; a chartwise etale; ∀ reduced closed C with pointImage = complement of pointImage b, pullback.snd a C is iso (equivalent by existence and uniqueness); pushout as ∃! t with a≫t=g ∧ b≫t=h. No extra hypotheses or universe restriction; edge cases (empty W/Z/V, identities, empty complement) covered. lean.statement verbatim; node changed only in lean; docstrings and sorry-only proof fine.
